The map $\Psi(x,y)=a(x)+b(y)-r$ has invertible derivative at zero. Reverse the parameter $y$ if needed to make its orientation positive. By [F1] its inverse is a smooth orientation-positive chart taking the alpha and beta arcs to the real and imaginary axes in $\mathbb C$. Pulling back the standard complex structure from that chart defines a smooth local structure $j_r$. It is compatible with $\eta$: in the chart $\eta=f(x,y)dx\wedge dy$ with $f>0$, so $\eta(v,j_rv)=f|v|^2>0$ and $\eta(j_rv,j_rw)=\eta(v,w)$. [F1, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.2 Conversely, if $B$ anticommutes with $J_0$ and has norm less than one, then $I-B$ is invertible and $$J_B=J_0(I+B)(I-B)^{-1}$$ is an almost complex structure. Indeed conjugation of the Cayley factor by $J_0$ replaces $B$ by $-B$ and therefore replaces that factor by its inverse, giving $J_B^2=-I$. The calculation of step 1.2 gives $\omega(v,J_Bv)>0$ for nonzero $v$. Consequently replacing $B$ by $rB$, $0\le r\le1$, joins the prescribed compatible $J_0$ to the original tame $J$ through tame structures, fixing either endpoint exactly. All expressions depend smoothly on the input operators and $r$ because their denominators remain invertible. [step 1.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 For $x=\{r_1,\ldots,r_m\}\in K$, choose disjoint small surface neighborhoods of its distinct coordinates and the charts from step 2.1. A nearby unordered tuple containing exactly one point in each of these neighborhoods has a unique ordering by the neighborhoods, giving the ordinary smooth off-diagonal product chart on $X$. In these coordinates $T_\alpha$ is $\mathbb R^m$ and $T_\beta$ is $i\mathbb R^m$, after assigning the beta indices to the corresponding factors. The product of the $j_{r_a}$ defines a local $J_{0,x}$, equal to $i$ in this chart and compatible with the descended product form, since its pullback is the sum of the positive two-dimensional compatible forms in step 2.1. By finiteness of $K$ shrink these neighborhoods to pairwise disjoint $U_x$ with compact closures avoiding the diagonal and all protected divisors. Such separation is possible because those sets are closed and disjoint from the finite $K$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Apply this formula on each $U_x$ with $J_0=J_{0,x}$ and the given background $J_t$. Choose a smooth cutoff $\chi_x$ supported compactly in $U_x$ and equal to one on a smaller neighborhood of $x$. Compute $B_t$ from step 1.2 and replace it by $(1-\chi_x)B_t$ in step 2.2. Its norm remains less than one. Where $\chi_x=1$ the resulting structure is exactly $J_{0,x}$, and where $\chi_x=0$ it is exactly $J_t$, so it glues smoothly to $J_t$ outside $U_x$. The finitely many supports are disjoint and avoid every protected set. Thus all modifications can be made simultaneously, are smooth in the family parameter, preserve tameness, and preserve every original value near the diagonal and protected divisors. [step 3.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

5.1 Finally a background exists here without an extension theorem: use $J=\operatorname{Sym}^m(j)$ itself on all of $X$. Off the diagonal its pullback is the product complex structure and is compatible with the product of $\eta$, because an orientation-compatible complex structure on a surface preserves its positive area form and makes $\eta(\cdot,j\cdot)$ positive symmetric. It therefore tames the descended form there. On the diagonal and protected divisors it already has exactly the required value by its definition as the given complex symmetric-product structure. Apply step 4.1 to this constant family to obtain $J_*$. The same argument proves the relative family assertion for any allowed background. These actual geometric constructions impose no genericity, universal submersion, Fredholm, or gluing conclusion on the resulting path. [step 3.1, step 4.1, given, construct, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The compact geometric bounds, actual equation, smooth convergence off zero, filled limit, and positive energy atom in the statement.

[F1] The local proof of [[lem-smooth-strip-compactness-away-from-energy-concentration]] extracts smooth limits off finitely many concentration points by countable energy limits, target-global epsilon estimates, actual chart bootstrap and countable diagonals. Proof.exact_text:
1.1 We fix a positive quantum once. The normalized bubble in [F2] has derivative norm one at a point and finite energy. The actual interior epsilon estimate at a fixed-radius disk about that point bounds its energy below by a positive constant $h_0$, independent of rescaling. Also every nonconstant autonomous sphere for a limiting target structure has energy at least $h_0$ after possibly decreasing $h_0$: choose a finite planar point with nonzero derivative, translate and dilate its source to make that norm one, and apply the same epsilon estimate. That estimate needs no global derivative bound for this lower bound; if its small-energy threshold fails it already supplies a positive lower bound. The structures $J_\infty(0,x)$ and their descendants retain the same uniform target bounds, so this quantum is uniform. Choose $h\le h_0$ also smaller than one eighth of the local-energy threshold in [F3]. [F2, F3, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 Write $M(r)=\lim_nE_g(u_n;B_r)$. Smooth convergence on compact annuli gives $M(r)-M(r')=E_g(u;B_r\setminus B_{r'})$ for $0<r'<r$ in the stated range. Letting $r'\downarrow0$ yields $$M(r)=m+E_g(u;B_r).$$ In particular it is continuous in $r$. For any centers $z_n\to0$, the inclusions $B_{r-\epsilon}\subset B_r(z_n)\subset B_{r+\epsilon}$ for large $n$ and then $\epsilon\downarrow0$ give $$\lim_n E_g(u_n;B_r(z_n))=m+E_g(u;B_r).$$ The same sandwich proves convergence on moving annuli of fixed positive radii to their $u$ energies. In particular energies of any shrinking disks have limsup at most $m$, by containment in arbitrarily small fixed disks. [given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Let $M_n=\max_{\overline{B_{1/2}}}|du_n|_g$ and choose a maximizing point $z_n$. After a subsequence $M_n\to\infty$ and $z_n\to0$. Otherwise a subsequence bounded on $B_{1/2}$, together with [F1], would converge smoothly also at zero, forcing its atom mass to vanish; smooth convergence away from zero forces any unbounded maximizing sequence toward zero. The local rescaling construction in [F2] produces a normalized plane bubble at zero: choose radii $r_n\to0$ with $r_nM_n\to\infty$ and $|z_n|/r_n\to0$, maximize $(r_n-|z|)|du_n(z)|$, and rescale by the gradient at that maximum. On expanding disks the rescaled derivative is at most two and equals one at the center; [F1] gives a smooth nonconstant plane limit. Its energy is at most $m$, because every fixed rescaled disk lies in an original disk shrinking to zero and energies of any fixed original disk tend to $m+E_g(u;B_r)$ by the established energy identity. By step 1.1 its energy is at least $h$, proving $m\ge h$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 Put $\mu=m-h/2>0$. For each large $n$ let $\rho_n$ be the smallest radius with $E_g(u_n;B_{\rho_n}(z_n))=\mu$, restricting to a small fixed disk contained in $B_1$. Such a radius exists: radius-zero energy is zero, energy varies continuously with radius, and step 1.2 makes the energy at any sufficiently small fixed radius eventually greater than $\mu$. The first solution is attained by continuity on a compact interval, so no strict monotonicity or uniqueness of all solutions is needed. The same fixed-radius argument gives $\rho_n\to0$. Define $v_n(w)=u_n(z_n+\rho_n w)$. Its domains contain each fixed planar disk eventually and its coefficient converges smoothly there to $J_\infty(0,x)$. Its energy on the unit disk is exactly $\mu$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 Apply the local extraction argument of [F1] to $v_n$ on an exhaustion of $\mathbb C$. Explicitly, diagonally extract limits of energies on a countable basis of disks and of total energies on exhaustion disks. Points at which every such neighborhood has limiting energy at least the epsilon threshold form a finite set: disjoint neighborhoods about any finite selection have total energy bounded by the original global bound, so their number is uniformly bounded. Away from that finite set the actual epsilon estimates give uniform first derivatives on smaller patches; compact target finite nets and a countable dense source set give local uniform convergence, and the actual local bootstrap then gives all derivative bounds and a countable smooth diagonal limit. Remove any exceptional point where a further subsequence has bounded gradients on one neighborhood, repeating at most finitely many times. Thus the remaining finite set $Z$ consists only of genuine gradient blowup points, and $v_n\to v$ smoothly on compact subsets of $\mathbb C\setminus Z$. Further countable extraction gives energy limits on small rational-radius disks about each $z\in Z$. [F1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

4.2 We now prove that no energy escaped at infinity in this rescaling. Fix a small original radius $d>0$. By step 1.2 and step 3.1, the annulus $$A_n=\{\rho_n<|z-z_n|<d\}$$ has limiting energy $h/2+E_g(u;B_d)$. Choose $d$ small enough that this is below half the neck threshold of [F3]; it remains below that threshold for all large $n$. Write $z=z_n+e^{\sigma+i\tau}$ on $A_n$. This is a holomorphic cylinder coordinate with period $2\pi$, and conformal invariance preserves energy. Its explicit source derivatives of $J_n(z_n+e^{\sigma+i\tau},x)$ are bounded by $Cd$, uniformly in $n$, so are below the [F3] variation threshold after reducing $d$. Uniform coefficient bounds of the needed orders persist. Every fixed-radius cylindrical patch has energy bounded by the total annulus energy. Apply [F3] after removing a unit buffer at each end. For $R\ge e^2$ and all large $n$ it gives $$\begin{aligned}E_g(u_n;B_{d/R}(z_n)\setminus B_{R\rho_n}(z_n))&\le C R^{-c},\\ \operatorname{diam}_g u_n(\overline{B_{d/R}(z_n)\setminus B_{R\rho_n}(z_n)})&\le C R^{-c/2},\end{aligned}$$ with constants independent of $d,R,n$ in this range. [F3, step 1.2, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Each $z\in Z$ has an atom $m_z\ge h$. To see this, repeat the local distance-weighted rescaling construction of step 2.1 in a small disk about that point. Its smooth normalized plane bubble has energy at least $h$ by step 1.1 and at most the atom mass by the disk containment argument of step 1.2. The limit $v$ has finite energy on $\mathbb C\setminus Z$ by exhaustion and the global bound. By [F2] it extends smoothly across the finitely many points of $Z$ and across infinity, hence is an autonomous holomorphic sphere. Annular smooth convergence and this extension show that energy limits on all small disks about each $z$ exist, not just rational ones, by the continuity/sandwich argument of step 1.2. This defines each $m_z$ independently of the chosen small radii. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

5.2 By the moving fixed-annulus convergence of step 1.2, the energy of $B_d(z_n)\setminus B_{d/R}(z_n)$ tends to $E_g(u;B_d\setminus B_{d/R})$. Hence step 4.2 gives, for every large $R$, $$m-CR^{-c}\le\liminf_n E_g(v_n;B_R)\le\limsup_n E_g(v_n;B_R)\le m+E_g(u;B_d).$$ The upper bound follows just by inclusion in $B_d(z_n)$. Letting $d\downarrow0$ proves the upper bound $m$; the lower bound is independent of $d$. A further countable radius diagonal, extended to other radii by the smooth annular convergence away $Z$, provides the indicated inner limits. The only remaining possible radii are the finitely many $|z|$ for $z\in Z$; extract their bounded energy sequences as well, so all fixed-radius inner limits exist. Then $R\to\infty$ proves $$\lim_{R\to\infty}\lim_nE_g(v_n;B_R)=m.$$ This is the actual energy capture statement. [step 1.2, step 4.1, step 4.2, algebra]

6.1 Choose $R$ larger than all $|z|$ for $z\in Z$ and avoiding any exceptional circle if needed. Partition $B_R$ into disjoint small disks about these points and their complement. Smooth convergence gives the complement energy, while the disk energies equal their atom masses plus the energy of the filled smooth limit, by the same annulus argument as step 1.2. Shrinking their radii and then letting $R\to\infty$ in step 5.2 yields $$E_g(v)+\sum_{z\in Z}m_z=m.$$ All sums are finite, so no exchange of an uncontrolled infinite sum with a limit occurs. [step 1.2, step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra]

6.2 The diameter estimate in step 4.2 proves the node connection. For fixed large $R$ outside $Z$, compare the two radial points $z_n+d/R$ and $z_n+R\rho_n$ in that closed annulus. Passage to $n\to\infty$ gives $$d_g(u(d/R),v(R))\le CR^{-c/2}.$$ First let $d\downarrow0$ using the filled original limit and then let $R\to\infty$ using the filled limit $v(\infty)$ from step 5.1. The inequality gives $u(0)=v(\infty)$. This proves actual connection of the two components, not merely equality of total energies. [step 5.1, step 4.2, algebra]

7.1 If $v$ is nonconstant, step 1.1 and step 6.1 give $E_g(v)\ge h$ and hence $m_z\le m-h$ for every child. Suppose $v$ is constant. Then $Z$ is nonempty by step 6.1. At any $z\in Z$ there are nearby points with $|dv_n|\to\infty$. The original center $z_n$ maximizes $|du_n|$ on $B_{1/2}$, and all fixed rescaled compact sets eventually lie there. Thus $|dv_n(0)|$ is at least these diverging values, so $0\in Z$. But $E_g(v_n;B_1)=\mu=m-h/2$ implies $m_0\le\mu<m$. If $Z$ had only this one point, step 6.1 would give $m_0=m$, a contradiction. Therefore $|Z|\ge2$; since each child mass is at least $h$, every child is at most $m-h$ in this case as well. This proves the stability and energy-drop assertions. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 All lower bounds, epsilon thresholds and neck constants used above depend only on compact target and uniform coefficient bounds. Subsequent rescalings have autonomous limits among the same pointwise structures and their explicit source derivatives decrease, so the same smaller $h$ remains valid. The construction involved finitely many choices of centers at each stage and countable extractions only; it therefore stays within Countable Choice. This completes the single soft-rescaling step with every claimed mass, limit and node property. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 7.1, construct] ∎

Statement.exact_text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(S,j_S)$ be a fixed closed compact Riemann surface, $(X,g)$ a compact smooth target, and $J_n(z,x)$ smooth families of almost complex structures converging smoothly on $S\times X$ to $J_\infty$. Let smooth solutions $u_n:S\to X$ of $du_n\circ j_S=J_n(z,u_n)\circ du_n$ have energies $E_g(u_n)\le E_0$.

After a subsequence there are a smooth base solution $u:S\to X$, a finite set $P\subset S$, and a finite rooted forest of sphere maps attached to $S$ at these points with the following properties. Every sphere lying over $p\in P$ is holomorphic for the autonomous target structure $J_\infty(p,\cdot)$. Child infinity is attached to a finite point of its parent sphere, or to $p$ on the base, and the component maps have equal values at every node. Distinct children of one component attach at distinct points. Every constant sphere has at least three nodes. The base maps converge smoothly off $P$, and each sphere map is a smooth local limit off its child attachment points after explicit compositions of complex translations and positive dilations in a fixed source chart. Relative child scales tend to zero and relative child centers tend to their attachment points.

There is no lost energy:
$$\lim_nE_g(u_n)=E_g(u)+\sum_vE_g(u_v).$$
The annuli connecting parent and child have vanishing energy and image diameter in the successive limits removing fixed neighborhoods of their two nodes. There is a uniform $h>0$ depending only on the compact geometric bounds such that the number of nonconstant sphere components is at most $\lfloor E_0/h\rfloor$ and the total number of sphere components is at most $2\lfloor E_0/h\rfloor$.

The source here is closed and fixed. Totally real boundary bubbling, strip breaking, variable source complex structures, and gluing are separate assertions.

Facts & Assumptions.exact_text:
**Given:** The compact fixed source and target, smooth coefficient convergence, actual solutions, and uniform energy bound of the statement.

[F1] The actual local proof of [[lem-smooth-strip-compactness-away-from-energy-concentration]] supplies countable concentration extraction and smooth local convergence away from finitely many points, by epsilon estimates and chart bootstrap. Its disk argument is local and therefore applies in the finitely many conformal charts of $S$.

[F2] [[lem-finite-energy-almost-complex-puncture-removability]] fills actual finite-energy interior punctures for smooth source-dependent coefficients, and fills finite-energy autonomous plane limits at infinity.

[F3] [[lem-soft-rescaling-captures-isolated-interior-energy-atoms]] proves an actual soft-rescaling step for an isolated atom of mass $m$. It gives a root sphere $v$, finitely many child atoms $m_z$, a uniform $h>0$, $E_g(v)+\sum m_z=m$, $h\le m_z\le m-h$, exact node connection, and smooth rescaled convergence off the child points. If the root is constant it has at least two children. Its proof also gives vanishing energy and image diameter on the connecting annuli and a lower bound $h$ for every nonconstant sphere.

Proof.exact_text:
1.1 Pass to a subsequence with total energies converging to $E\le E_0$. Cover the compact source by finitely many relatively compact conformal charts and choose a countable basis of disks in them. The smooth convergence of $J_n$ gives uniform coefficient bounds. Apply the concentration argument of [F1]: extract energy limits on the countable basis, declare a point exceptional only when every basis neighborhood has limiting energy at least a fixed epsilon threshold, and use disjoint neighborhoods and the total bound $E_0$ to bound the number of exceptional points. Away from them actual epsilon estimates give first derivative bounds, compact target finite nets and dense source points give locally uniform subsequences, and the local higher bootstrap and a countable derivative diagonal give smooth convergence to a solution $u$. Exceptional points where a further subsequence has bounded gradients on a neighborhood are removed, at most finitely many times. Thus the remaining finite set $P$ consists of genuine concentration points. This uses finitely many charts and countably many extractions, not arbitrary choice. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 The limit has energy at most $E_0$ on $S\setminus P$ by exhaustion and smooth convergence. By [F2] it extends smoothly across every point of $P$, with equation for $J_\infty$. In disjoint coordinate disks about those points, extract limits of the energies on rational concentric radii. Smooth convergence on annuli and the filled base show that these limits extend to all sufficiently small radii and have form $$\lim_nE_g(u_n;B_r(p))=m_p+E_g(u;B_r(p)).$$ Indeed subtract two rational-radius limits, pass to the annular smooth limit, and let the inner radius decrease to zero; continuity and monotone sandwiches extend to other radii. The masses $m_p$ are positive and at least $h$: if one were below the uniform bubble quantum, the local normalized blowup construction in [F3] would produce a nonconstant bubble of energy at most $m_p$ and at least $h$, a contradiction. A point with zero mass has a neighborhood below the epsilon threshold and is not a genuine concentration point. After decreasing $h$ uniformly over the finite chart cover, it is the same constant as in [F3]. [F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Remove the finitely many disjoint radius-$r$ disks from the source. Smooth convergence on the remaining compact surface gives its energy, while step 2.1 gives each disk energy. Add these equalities and let $r\downarrow0$. The base is smooth and the disks have vanishing base energy, so $$E=E_g(u)+\sum_{p\in P}m_p.$$ This separates every original atom from the base by an actual finite partition and accounts for all energy on the closed source. No compactness assertion at an unbounded end has been used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 We prove by induction on $N=\lfloor m/h\rfloor\ge1$ that any isolated interior atom of mass $m$ in these data is represented by a finite sphere tree of total energy $m$, connected to its given filled parent value. Apply [F3] to that atom. Its root sphere is connected to the parent, its distinct child points form a finite set $Z$, and its child masses obey $h\le m_z\le m-h$. Thus $\lfloor m_z/h\rfloor\le N-1$. If $N=1$ there can be no child mass, because $m-h<h$; the root itself is the required sphere tree. If $N>1$, restrict the rescaled sequence to disjoint small coordinate disks about its finitely many child points. Their filled limiting parent map is the smooth root sphere, their coefficients converge smoothly to the same autonomous structure, their isolated masses are $m_z$, and their energies have exactly the bounds required by [F3]. The induction hypothesis therefore supplies a finite tree for each child, connected at the prescribed point. Their total energy plus that of the root is $E_g(v)+\sum m_z=m$. Finitely many subsequence extractions suffice at this node. Finite depth, bounded by $N$, and finite branching prove that the entire process terminates. [F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 The induction constructs actual reparametrizations and all required scale relations. At a root, [F3] uses the affine map $w\mapsto z_n+\rho_n w$ in a fixed original conformal chart, with $\rho_n>0$ tending to zero. At a child in the parent's plane coordinate, it uses $w\mapsto a_n+r_n w$, where $a_n\to a$ is its finite attachment point and $r_n\to0$. Composition with the parent's map remains a complex translation and positive dilation in that original chart. The ratio of original child to parent scales is $r_n\to0$, and the relative center tends to $a$. Siblings have distinct limiting centers because [F3] extracts distinct concentration points on a parent. The convergence off the finite child set at each vertex is exactly the actual local smooth convergence in [F3]. Since the constructed forest is finite, pass to the finitely many nested subsequences and retain all earlier component limits. [F3, step 3.2, construct, algebra]

4.2 A constant root created in [F3] has at least two children, hence at least three nodes after adding its parent attachment at infinity. This remains true at every depth, so every constant sphere is stable. Each nonconstant sphere has energy at least $h$, and the tree energy identities together with step 3.1 imply that their number $A$ is at most $\lfloor E_0/h\rfloor$. Let $G$ be the number of constant spheres and $q=|P|$ the number of nonempty trees. In this forest the number of parent-child edges among sphere vertices is $A+G-q$, while each constant vertex has at least two children and each other vertex has nonnegative child count. Thus $A+G-q\ge2G$, so $G\le A-q$. If the forest is empty there is nothing to count; otherwise the total number of sphere vertices is at most $2A-q\le2\lfloor E_0/h\rfloor$. [F3, step 3.1, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 Every parent-child pair has equal nodal values by the node-connection assertion of [F3]. Its explicit cylindrical-annulus estimates also give vanishing energy and image diameter between the two components: first take the sequence limit with fixed outer parent-node radius and fixed inner child-plane radius, then shrink the former and enlarge the latter. At a deeper edge the same estimates hold in that parent's conformal coordinate, and composition with earlier affine changes preserves source conformality and energy. There are finitely many edges, so all these successive limiting conclusions hold simultaneously. Gluing the component domains only at these matched points gives a continuous map from the finite nodal surface. This describes a limit, not a smoothing or gluing construction. [F3, step 3.2, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 Apply step 3.2 to each original atom $m_p$. Their finitely many trees attach to the smooth base at distinct points $p$. Step 5.1 proves continuity and the asserted convergence and annulus properties; summing their actual energy identities in step 3.1 gives $$\lim_nE_g(u_n)=E_g(u)+\sum_vE_g(u_v).$$ All sphere structures over $p$ are $J_\infty(p,x)$, since their source coordinates tend to $p$ and every further rescaling freezes the same coefficient. Step 4.2 proves the bounds and stability. This completes the actual fixed-source interior bubble-tree compactness statement under Countable Choice, without importing boundary compactification, strip breaking or gluing. [step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 4.2, algebra] ∎

Statement.exact_text:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,g)$ be compact and $L\subset X$ a fixed compact totally real submanifold. On the closed upper half-disk let smooth almost complex families $J_n(z,x)$ converge smoothly locally to $J_\infty$, with uniform coefficient bounds, and suppose $J_n(s,x)=J_b(x)$ for real $s$ and $x\in L$, independent of $n,s$. Let smooth solutions $u_n:B_1^+\to X$, smooth up to the straight boundary with values there on $L$, have uniformly bounded energy and converge smoothly locally off $0$, including boundary points, to a solution $u$ smoothly filled at $0$. Suppose concentric half-disk energies have limits with positive atom mass $m$ at $0$.

There is a uniform $h>0$ such that $m\ge h$ and, after a subsequence, real centers $a_n\to0$, positive scales $\rho_n\to0$, an autonomous $J_\infty(0,x)$-holomorphic disk $v$ with boundary on $L$, and finitely many child atoms $Z\subset\overline{\mathbb H}$ have these properties. The rescaled maps $v_n(w)=u_n(a_n+\rho_nw)$ converge smoothly locally off $Z$ to $v$, on the upper half-plane including its straight boundary. Moreover
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\lim_nE_g(v_n;B_R^+)=m=E_g(v)+\sum_{z\in Z}m_z,\qquad v(\infty)=u(0).$$
Every child has mass at least $h$. Boundary children satisfy $m_z\le m-h$; interior children satisfy $m_z\le m$. If $v$ is constant then
$$|Z\cap\mathbb R|+2|Z\cap\mathbb H|\ge2.$$
Thus the constant disk is stable after including its parent boundary node at infinity. The connecting half-annuli have vanishing energy and image diameter. The same $h$ works for descendants. These conclusions constitute one actual boundary soft-rescaling step.
